entities.summary:
Guillaume de la Sudrie, a French Dominican and Cardinal, played a pivotal role in shaping the religious landscape of Western Europe during the late Middle Ages. Born in Laguenne, Corrèze, around 1320, he rose through the ranks of the Dominican Order to become a prominent figure in the Catholic Church. De la Sudrie's influence extended beyond his ecclesiastical duties, as he participated in the complex web of alliances and rivalries between European powers during this period.

As bishop of Marseille, he worked to consolidate the city's power and influence within the region. De la Sudrie's tenure was marked by a series of diplomatic missions and negotiations with neighboring kingdoms, including the Kingdom of France and the Papal States.

Despite the challenges posed by the Black Death, which ravaged Europe in the late 14th century, de la Sudrie's legacy endured. He was canonized as a saint by the Catholic Church in 1488, cementing his place in the annals of Christian history.

His influence can still be felt today, as the institutions and traditions he helped shape continue to shape the spiritual lives of millions around the world.

The cardinal's commitment to his faith and his community remains an inspiration to scholars and historians seeking to understand the complexities of medieval Europe.
